steps.headline: Cards, design a: stars first, Easy setup a normal tag, family as one plain grey line.
steps.changed: Stars lead the chip row; Easy setup is a normal tag with an explainer; "Why it's here" moved into the (i).
steps.notice: Each family line now reads in plain words, like "A modified version of Firefox that keeps up with its updates".

steps.headline: On phones, cards are short rows: about 4 per screen instead of 1½.
steps.changed: Small picture, name, one sideways chip row (stars first), one line of description.

steps.headline: Tapping a tag or the (i) explains what it means and why the project is listed there.
steps.changed: A small pop-up from the tag.
steps.notice: Nothing else on the card changes.

steps.headline: Project page: buttons back on the right, the claim line, and a Family card with plain-words relations.
steps.changed: The three buttons sit at the right of the top card. "This listing is managed by r/TrueOpenSource…" sits under the description. Family is its own card.
steps.notice: The claim line disappears once a developer claims the page.

steps.headline: Each family row's (i) gives the one-sentence reason and its source.
On phones the Family section starts folded.
Search results: stars first, no "Open project" or "Strong match" tags, pictures lined up.
steps.changed: A group shows "24 open options"; a closed app says "Closed app"; every project shows stars, devices and its group.

steps.headline: The same on phones.
steps.changed: One sideways chip row per result.

steps.headline: Most requested: the top three as cards, each named by its job, with "Like LinkedIn" underneath.
steps.changed: The confusing kind tags are gone; a request for LinkedIn counts toward Professional networking.
steps.notice: Names and numbers are pretend preview data.

steps.headline: Home shows the five most requested as five equal cards.

steps.notice: All three use the full width, plain words (no "proof file"), and open by saying what claiming gives you. Pick the same letter on each slide, or mix if one step looks better in another design.
